The demonstrations are part of a wider European unrest which includes protests in Belgium, Albania, Greece, Italy, Portugal, Spain, Austria, Ireland, Serbia and Germany. The movement is marked by demonstrations and high school blockades. Explaining the protests, students have cited teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms, run-down buildings, and limited public investment in social programs and infrastructure. Students noted stress linked to the university application website Parcoursup and high temperatures in classrooms that reached up to 40 °C (104 °F) during the 2026 European heatwaves. Protesters in France and across Europe complained of high inflation, rents, fuel costs, and unemployment, coupled with social spending cuts. The initial police response used a variety of forceful crowd-control weapons, resulting in serious injuries, including to children, and violent conflict between police and protestors have led to 6,800 arrests, most of them of minors.
